items.greek: Ὁ τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς δημιουργὸς καὶ πατὴρ οὐ δεῖται αἵματος οὐδὲ κνίσσης οὐδὲ τῆς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθῶν καὶ θυμιαμάτων εὐωδίας, αὐτὸς ὢν ἡ τελεία εὐωδία, ἀνενδεὴς καὶ ἀπροσδεής.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 58 (Greek), PDF p. 142; Greek read from the 160 dpi page image.
items.english: the Framer and Father of this universe does not need blood, nor the odour of burnt-offerings, nor the fragrance of flowers and incense, forasmuch as He is Himself perfect fragrance, needing nothing either within or without;
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 58 (Greek) = PDF p. 142; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: God the Framer and Father needs no sacrifice because he is self-sufficient.
items.limits: Shows God as self-sufficient (no needs), a metaphysical premise, not a Trinitarian statement. Says nothing about the Son or Spirit. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.greek: δι᾽ ἐκείνους καὶ ἡμεῖς, οἱ διακρίνοντες καὶ χωρίζοντες τὸ ἀγένητον καὶ τὸ γενητόν, τὸ ὂν καὶ τὸ οὐκ ὄν, τὸ νοητὸν καὶ τὸ αἰσθητόν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὸ προσῆκον ὄνομα ἀποδιδόντες, προσελευσόμεθα καὶ προσκυνήσομεν τὰ ἀγάλματα;
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 66 (Greek), PDF p. 150; checked at 400 dpi crop. Spelling ἀγένητον (one ν) as printed.
items.english: are we therefore, who do distinguish and separate the uncreated and the created, that which is and that which is not, that which is apprehended by the understanding and that which is perceived by the senses, and who give the fitting name to each of them — are we to come and worship images?
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 66 (Greek) = PDF p. 150; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Christians distinguish uncreated from created, and matter from God, so they do not worship images of matter.
items.limits: Creator/creature distinction only; no Logos, Son or Spirit. Argument against idolatry, not a Triad statement.

items.greek: ὁ δὲ κόσμος οὐχ ὡς δεομένου τοῦ θεοῦ γέγονεν· πάντα γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἐστιν αὐτὸς αὐτῷ, φῶς ἀπρόσιτον, κόσμος τέλειος, πνεῦμα, δύναμις, λόγος.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 70 (Greek), PDF p. 154; read from 160 dpi image.
items.english: But the world was not created because God needed it; for God is Himself everything to Himself — light unapproachable, a perfect world, spirit, power, reason.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 70 (Greek) = PDF p. 154; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: God is himself the light, world, spirit, power and reason, and needs nothing outside himself.
items.limits: Lists 'spirit, power, reason' as attributes of the one God ('God is himself everything to himself'), with no personal distinction. Unitarian and Sabellian readers cite it for an attribute reading; Trinitarian readers see a preparation for Logos and Spirit. Only this list is shown, not a person-language statement. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.greek: οὕτως ἑνὶ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ λόγῳ υἱῷ νοουμένῳ ἀμερίστῳ πάντα ὑποτέτακται.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 84 (Greek), PDF p. 168; read from 160 dpi image. Otto's note 16: Maranus/Bodl. 1-2/Aet. read ἑνὶ θεῷ; Otto keeps ἑνὶ τῷ θεῷ and glosses 'ita uni nempe deo eiusque logo'.
items.english: so to the one God and the Logos proceeding from Him, the Son, apprehended by us as inseparable from Him, all things are in like manner subjected.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 84 (Greek) = PDF p. 168; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: The one God and his Logos from him, the Son, conceived as indivisible, are the powers over which all things are subject.
items.limits: Good for a Son-as-Logos reading. But the Greek has no word for 'proceeding' (ANF renders παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ), and 'conceived' (νοουμένῳ) is ours not theirs. Subordinationist (Arian) readers take it as Logos below the one God. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.greek: καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τῆς ὕλης κεχωρηκὸς κατὰ τὰς παραλλάξεις αὐτῆς ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο ὄνομα μεταλαγχάνειν φατέ, σῶμα μὲν τὰ εἴδη τῆς ὕλης τοῦ θεοῦ γενήσεται, φθειρομένων δὲ τῶν στοιχείων κατὰ τὴν ἐκπύρωσιν ἀνάγκη συμφθαρῆναι ὁμοῦ τοῖς εἴδεσι τὰ ὀνόματα, μόνον μένοντος τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 108 (Greek), PDF p. 192; read from 160 dpi image. φατέ = 'you say' (addressed to the Stoics).
items.english: ...and say that the Spirit of God, which pervades matter, obtains according to its variations a diversity of names, the forms of matter will become the body of God; but when the elements are destroyed in the conflagration, the names will necessarily perish along with the forms, the Spirit of God alone remaining.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 108 (Greek) = PDF p. 192; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Athenagoras refutes the Stoic 'Spirit of God pervading matter' view, which would make matter God's body.
items.limits: This is the Stoics' doctrine ('you say'), not his own; the pneuma is impersonal and pervades matter. It does not show a Holy Spirit as a person. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.ref: Leg. 24 (Otto 24 = ANF 24; no section numbers; sentence in the first half of ch. 24)
items.greek: Ὡς γὰρ θεὸν φαμεν καὶ υἱὸν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ καὶ πνεῦμα ἅγιον, ἑνούμενα μὲν κατὰ δύναμιν τὸν πατέρα τὸν υἱὸν τὸ πνεῦμα, ὅτι νοῦς λόγος σοφία ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ πατρός, καὶ ἀπόῤῥοια ὡς φῶς ἀπὸ πυρὸς τὸ πνεῦμα, οὕτως καὶ ἑτέρας εἶναι δυνάμεις κατειλήμμεθα περὶ τὴν ὕλην ἀρχούσας καὶ δι᾽ αὐτῆς.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 124 (Greek), PDF p. 208; 300 dpi crop checked. Otto's apparatus n.7 reads ὅτι (not ὅτε); n.9 says the codices and editions read ἐχούσας and Otto prints ἀρχούσας as Maranus's conjecture. Migne PG 6 OCR (archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_006) reads κατὰ δύναμιν, ὅτι Νοῦς, Λόγος, Σοφία, Υἱὸς τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ ἀπόῤῥοια, ὡς φῶς ἀπὸ πυρὸς, τὸ Πνεῦμα, same as Otto; Migne prints ἐχούσας.
items.english: as we acknowledge a God, and a Son his Logos, and a Holy Spirit, united in essence — the Father, the Son, the Spirit, because the Son is the Intelligence, Reason, Wisdom of the Father, and the Spirit an effluence, as light from fire; so also do we apprehend the existence of other powers, which exercise dominion about matter, and by means of it,
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 124 (Greek) = PDF p. 208; Otto Latin p. 125 = PDF p. 209 ('secundum potentiam'); ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Athenagoras confesses God, the Son his Logos and the Holy Spirit, united in power, the Son as the Father's mind, reason and wisdom, and the Spirit as an effluence like light from fire.
items.limits: ANF's 'united in essence' is NOT in the Greek: κατὰ δύναμιν means 'in power' (Otto's Latin p. 125 says 'secundum potentiam'; Migne OCR agrees). The text speaks of unity 'in power', not sharing one essence, so it does not state homoousios. The Son is named Logos/Wisdom of the Father (subordination language). Sabellians cite the 'unity' and the Spirit-as-effluence; Arians cite 'the Son is the Father's mind/wisdom'. The sentence sits in an angelology discussion. ANF must not be quoted for 'essence'.

items.greek: ἐναντίον ἐστὶ τὸ περὶ τὴν ὕλην ἔχον πνεῦμα, γενόμενον μὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, καθὸ οἱ λοιποὶ ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ γεγόνασιν ἄγγελοι, καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τῇ ὕλῃ καὶ τοῖς τῆς ὕλης εἴδεσι πιστευσάμενον διοίκησιν.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 126 (Greek), PDF p. 210; 300 dpi crop checked for the first half, 160 dpi for the rest.
items.english: ...the spirit which is about matter, who was created by God, just as the other angels were created by Him, and entrusted with the control of matter and the forms of matter, is opposed.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 126 (Greek) = PDF p. 210; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: The angelic ruler of matter, opposed to God's good, is himself created by God, like the other angels.
items.limits: Angels are creatures, not divine. Shows angelology, not Trinitarian doctrine. The word πνεῦμα is used for a created spirit here, a caution for reading Spirit passages.

items.ref: Leg. 24 (Otto 24 = ANF 24; no section numbers; printed pp. 126-128)
items.greek: Τοῦτο γὰρ ἡ τῶν ἀγγέλων σύστασις, τῷ θεῷ ἐπὶ προνοίᾳ γεγονέναι τοῖς ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ διακεκοσμημένοις, ἵνα τὴν μὲν παντελικὴν καὶ γενικὴν ὁ θεὸς ἔχῃ τῶν ὅλων πρόνοιαν, τὴν δὲ ἐπὶ μέρους οἱ ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς ταχθέντες ἄγγελοι.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed pp. 126-128 (Greek), PDF pp. 210-212; read from 160 dpi images.
items.english: For this is the office of the angels — to exercise providence for God over the things created and ordered by Him; so that God may have the universal and general providence of the whole, while the particular parts are provided for by the angels appointed over them.
items.page: Otto 1857 pp. 126-128 (Greek) = PDF pp. 210-212; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Angels exercise particular providence under God's universal providence.
items.limits: ANF renders σύστασις as 'office'; the Greek word is closer to 'constitution/establishment'. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked. Angels are creatures, not Persons.

items.ref: Leg. 24 (Otto 24 = ANF 24; no section numbers; printed pp. 128-130)
items.greek: μὲν γὰρ ἄλλοι, αὐθαίρετοι δὴ οἷοι γεγόνασιν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἔμειναν ἐφ᾽ οἷς αὐτοὺς ἐποίησεν καὶ διέταξεν ὁ θεός, οἱ δὲ ἐνύβρισαν καὶ τῇ τῆς οὐσίας ὑποστάσει καὶ τῇ ἀρχῇ, οὗτός τε ὁ τῆς ὕλης καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰδῶν ἄρχων καὶ ἕτεροι τῶν περὶ τὸ πρῶτον τοῦτο στερέωμα, (ἴστε δὲ μηδὲν ἡμᾶς ἀμάρτυρον λέγειν, ἃ δὲ τοῖς προφήταις ἐκπεφώνηται μηνύειν) ἐκεῖνοι μὲν εἰς ἐπιθυμίαν πεσόντες παρθένων καὶ ἥττονες σαρκὸς εὑρεθέντες, οὗτος δὲ ἀμελήσας καὶ πονηρὸς περὶ τὴν τῶν πεπιστευμένων γενόμενος διοίκησιν. Ἐκ μὲν οὖν τῶν περὶ τὰς παρθένους ἐχόντων οἱ καλούμενοι ἐγεννήθησαν γίγαντες.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed pp. 128-130 (Greek), PDF pp. 212-214; 300 dpi crops checked for the giants and fall sentences.
items.english: Some, free agents, you will observe, such as they were created by God, continued in those things for which God had made and over which He had ordained them; but some outraged both the constitution of their nature and the government entrusted to them: namely, this ruler of matter and its various forms, and others of those who were placed about this first firmament (you know that we say nothing without witnesses, but state the things which have been declared by the prophets); these fell into impure love of virgins, and were subjugated by the flesh, and he became negligent and wicked in the management of the things entrusted to him. Of these lovers of virgins, therefore, were begotten those who are called giants.
items.page: Otto 1857 pp. 128-130 (Greek) = PDF pp. 212-214; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Some angels, free, fell into lust for women and begat the giants; the angelic ruler of matter was negligent and wicked.
items.limits: A fall-of-angels and Genesis 6 account, appealing to the prophets; not a Trinitarian passage. ANF's 'lovers of virgins' loosely renders περὶ τὰς παρθένους ἐχόντων (literally 'those concerned with virgins'). Critics of Nicene framing point to this as angelology not found in Nicene doctrine; no scholar is cited here (not verified in this brief).

items.greek: Οὗτοι τοίνυν οἱ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἐκπεσόντες τῶν οὐρανῶν, περὶ τὸν ἀέρα ἔχοντες καὶ τὴν γῆν, οὐκέτι εἰς τὰ ὑπερουράνια ὑπερκύψαι δυνάμενοι, καὶ αἱ τῶν γιγάντων ψυχαὶ οἱ περὶ τὸν κόσμον εἰσὶ πλανώμενοι δαίμονες, ὁμοίας κινήσεις, οἱ μὲν αἷς ἔλαβον συστάσεσιν, οἱ δαίμονες, οἱ δὲ αἷς ἔσχον ἐπιθυμίαις, οἱ ἄγγελοι, ποιούμενοι.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 130 (Greek) / 132 (Greek), PDF pp. 214 and 216; read from 160 dpi. Otto's note 3: some MSS read οἱ γίγαντες for οἱ δαίμονες.
items.english: These angels, then, who have fallen from heaven, and haunt the air and the earth, and are no longer able to rise to heavenly things, and the souls of the giants, which are the demons who wander about the world, perform actions similar, the one (that is, the demons) to the natures they have received, the other (that is, the angels) to the appetites they have indulged.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 130 (Greek) = PDF p. 214; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: The fallen angels roam air and earth and cannot rise to heaven; the giants' souls are wandering demons.
items.limits: Greek read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked. The ANF's bracketed glosses (that is, the demons / the angels) are the translator's. Hard for Nicene readers, since it is demonology, not Trinity; it is cited by critics of the early apologists.

items.greek: Ἀλλ᾽ ἐπεὶ αἱ ἀπὸ τοὐναντίου πνεύματος δαιμονικαὶ κινήσεις καὶ ἐνέργειαι τὰς ἀτάκτους ταύτας ἐπιφορὰς παρέχουσιν, ἤδη καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἄλλον ἄλλως, καὶ καθ᾽ ἕνα καὶ κατὰ ἔθνη, μερικῶς καὶ κοινῶς, κατὰ τὸν τῆς ὕλης λόγον καὶ τῆς πρὸς τὰ θεῖα συμπαθείας, ἐνδοθεν καὶ ἐξωθεν κινοῦσαι.
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 136 (Greek), PDF p. 220; read from 160 dpi image.
items.english: But because the demoniac movements and operations proceeding from the adverse spirit produce these disorderly sallies, and moreover move men, some in one way and some in another, as individuals and as nations, separately and in common, in accordance with the tendency of matter on the one hand, and of the affinity for divine things on the other, from within and from without
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 136 (Greek) = PDF p. 220; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Demonic spirit ('from the opposite spirit') moves men inwardly and outwardly.
items.limits: Same word πνεῦμα, here an evil demonic spirit: a warning that 'spirit' does not by itself mean the Holy Spirit. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.greek: Ἀλλὰ θεὸν μὲν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ κόσμου ἄγει, δαίμονας δὲ οὐσίας νοεῖ ψυχικάς, καὶ ἥρωας τὰς κεχωρισμένας ψυχὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀγαθοὺς μὲν τὰς ἀγαθάς, κακοὺς δὲ τὰς φαύλας. Πλάτωνι δέ, τὰ ἄλλα ἐπέχων, καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς τε τὸν ἀγένητον θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγενήτου εἰς κόσμον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γεγονότας, τούς τε πλανήτας καὶ τοὺς ἀπλανεῖς ἀστέρας, καὶ εἰς δαίμονας τέμνει·
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 118 (Greek), PDF p. 202; 300 dpi crop checked for the Plato sentence. Otto's apparatus n.9 discusses the spelling ἀγένητον/ἀγέννητον.
items.english: First Thales, as those who have accurately examined his opinions report, divides [superior beings] into God, demons, and heroes. God he recognises as the Intelligence (νοῦς) of the world; by demons he understands beings possessed of soul; and by heroes the separated souls of men, the good being the good souls, and the bad the worthless. Plato again, while withholding his assent on other points, also divides [superior beings] into the uncreated God and those produced by the uncreated One for the adornment of heaven, the planets, and the fixed stars, and into demons
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 118 (Greek) = PDF p. 202; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Thales and Plato sort the superior beings into God, demons and heroes, and Plato's 'uncreated God' and created beings.
items.limits: A classification of superior beings by pagan philosophers, reported by Athenagoras. Shows the 'uncreated/created' vocabulary, not a Christian triad. Athenagoras's own view is not in the Greek here. ANF's bracketed '[superior beings]' is the translator's.

items.greek: καὶ περὶ δύο καὶ τρία, δεύτερον δὲ περὶ τὰ δεύτερα, καὶ τρίτον περὶ τὰ τρίτα, περὶ τῶν ἐκ τῶν αἰσθητῶν γῆς τε καὶ οὐρανοῦ λεγομένων γεγονέναι μεῖζον ἢ καθ᾽ ἑαυτὸν τάληθὲς μαθεῖν ἐνόμισεν;
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 120 (Greek), PDF p. 204; read from 160 dpi image. The sentence is a question.
items.english: ...and about two and three, that He is the second moving about the seconds, and the third about the thirds; — did this man think, that to learn the truth concerning those who are said to have been produced from sensible things, namely earth and heaven, was a task transcending his powers?
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 120 (Greek) = PDF p. 204; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: Athenagoras reports Plato's 'two and three' ordering (second about seconds, third about thirds) as part of Plato's knowledge of God.
items.limits: A Platonic ordering, not a Christian triad; no word τριάς occurs. The Greek has no verb of motion: ANF's 'moving' is the translator's addition. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.

items.greek: Καὶ οἱ μὲν περὶ τὰ εἴδωλα αὐτοὺς ἕλκοντες οἱ δαίμονές εἰσιν οἱ προειρημένοι, οἱ προστετηκότες τῷ ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερείων αἵματι καὶ ταῦτα περιλιχμώμενοι· οἱ δὲ τοῖς πολλοῖς ἀρέσκοντες θεοὶ καὶ ταῖς εἰκόσιν ἐπονομαζόμενοι,
items.greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum vol. 7 (Athenagoras), Jena: Mauke 1857; archive.org id athenagoraephilo00athe, PDF read by page image (renders at 160-600 dpi) plus OCR text layer. Otto printed p. 136 (Greek, heading 26), PDF p. 220; read from 160 dpi image.
items.english: They who draw men to idols, then, are the aforesaid demons, who are eager for the blood of the sacrifices, and lick them; but the gods that please the multitude, and whose names are given to the images, were men, as may be learned from their history.
items.page: Otto 1857 p. 136 (Greek) = PDF p. 220; ANF page unknown
items.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (public domain); newadvent.org transcription
items.what_it_says: The demons draw men to idols; the gods of the multitude were men.
items.limits: Demonology against idols, not Trinitarian; shows that the angels/demons are creatures. Read at 160 dpi, not crop-checked.
